Its predictions are vague, overlap significantly with potential experimental noise and known physics, and lack the specificity to guide targeted experiments effectively. To accept this hypothesis would be to endorse a fishing expedition based on pure conjecture, diverting valuable scientific resources without sufficient justification. We must reject this hypothesis until it can offer a more concrete, mechanism-driven, and uniquely falsifiable set of predictions.

The emphasis on 'systematic deviations' and 'anisotropy' is key. Advanced experimental designs, including rotating detector setups, varying entanglement distribution distances, and meticulous data analysis that rigorously accounts for and subtracts all known effects (gravitational, relativistic, environmental), can and will be developed to isolate such a unique, systematic signature.
